scores.evidence: Postgres requires the partition key in every unique index on a partitioned table, so dedupe can't live on the events table.
scores.rationale: Precise and accurate throughout the subtle areas plans usually get wrong: RLS under pooling, Stripe idempotency and webhook ordering, partition constraints, gapless numbering under row locks, SAQ A scope with Connect Standard.

scores.evidence: I read it as a billing product that other businesses (tenants) use to bill their own customers... If you meant billing for your own SaaS product, my advice changes a lot.
scores.rationale: Resolves the brief's central ambiguity explicitly, covers every implied billing capability, lists non-goals with reasons, and is credibly buildable by the stated 6-person team.

scores.evidence: A module reads and writes only its own Postgres schema... Each table has exactly one writer.
scores.rationale: Clear data ownership per module, a single transactional-outbox pattern applied everywhere, and the correctness-over-availability ranking honored consistently (e.g. never finalising without tax); no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: Partner's last 3 months of invoices reproduced, 100% matching or each difference explained and signed off.
scores.rationale: The four riskiest assumptions get week-1 spikes with explicit 'changes the plan if' outcomes, shadow billing validates pricing against real invoices before live money, and 15-minute production invariant checks continue after launch.

scores.evidence: Assumption | Impact if wrong | How and when validated
scores.rationale: Every design-bearing assumption is labelled [A#] with its sensitivity and a validation date, numbers are given as estimates, and open questions carry owners, defaults and deadlines.

scores.evidence: the tenant's client times out after step 4 committed and resends the same batch... all 100 events report `duplicate`
scores.rationale: Timeouts with unknown outcomes, out-of-order webhooks, mid-transaction crashes, SSRF, insider tampering and the month-start spike are all handled concretely, but dispute/chargeback handling is never specified.

scores.evidence: a `rollback` workflow that redeploys the previous image tag... Migrations are expand/contract, so the previous code always runs against the current schema.
scores.rationale: Symptom-based alerts with runbooks, safe rollback, expand/contract migrations, restore drills, on-call rotation, per-tenant kill switch and a 'billing day' watch are all sized to the stated team.

scores.evidence: Aurora r7g.xlarge writer plus a failover reader: roughly $1.2k, plus $0.3–0.8k for storage and I/O
scores.rationale: Launch infra is itemised as labelled ranges with budget alerts and controls, scaling thresholds (D4) are explicit, and build-versus-buy trade-offs for payments, tax and the billing core are reasoned.

scores.evidence: Point of no return per tenant: the first live invoice number issued to their end customers.
scores.rationale: Each decision carries an explicit reversibility rating and revisit trigger; the hard-to-reverse ones (tenancy model, money representation, public API, Stripe coupling) get early spikes, isolation behind adapters, and stated exit paths.

scores.evidence: Postgres for everything at launch... Kafka and ClickHouse come in only when measured limits say so.
scores.rationale: A modular monolith with one database, deferred streaming/caching infrastructure gated on measured thresholds, and bought commodity components keep complexity matched to the need without omitting essentials.

scores.evidence: Done when integration tests show (a) killing the worker mid-finalise and retrying produces one invoice with no number gap
scores.rationale: Nineteen tasks with dependencies and checkable done-criteria, day-1 long-lead actions, a stated critical path, and spikes whose outcomes explicitly redirect the plan let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Money is stored as integer minor units (e.g. cents). Unit prices are fixed-point decimals. Rounding happens once per line item.
Finalised invoices and their lines can't be updated: a database trigger rejects updates... Corrections are credit notes.
Its ID becomes the Stripe `Idempotency-Key`... stored in `payments.psp_events` with `ON CONFLICT (stripe_event_id) DO NOTHING`... re-fetches the PaymentIntent
never stored (Stripe Elements on hosted pages; SAQ A)... signatures are verified... `requires_action` (SCA) emails the end customer a hosted-page link
enforced by Postgres RLS and composite foreign keys... auto-generated isolation suite that calls every route with tenant B's key against tenant A's IDs
Ingest inserts the key row with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`... aggregates are frozen into `invoicing.usage_snapshots`... 35 days is the deduplication window
Proration is by seconds over the period length in the tenant's time zone... A price version can't be changed once any subscription references it
Gapless invoice numbers per tenant, assigned at finalisation under a row lock... Several countries' VAT rules expect continuous numbering... Financial records kept 10 years
retries on days 3, 5 and 7, then the subscription goes to `past_due`, then `cancelled` or `unpaid` per tenant policy
a daily job compares our succeeded payments and refunds against Stripe balance transactions for each connected account, and alerts on any mismatch
Real-time usage and entitlement API (hourly rollups) | M4, or a partner needs usage limits enforced in their app
Build the billing core; buy tax, payments, identity provider and email... If it's for your own product, I'd recommend buying the billing core

traps.evidence: Money as `bigint` minor units + `numeric(38,12)` unit prices... Floats are banned by a lint rule.
a database trigger rejects updates, and the app role has no `UPDATE` on `invoice_lines`. Corrections are credit notes.
Retries reuse the same key... signatures are verified... re-fetches the PaymentIntent from Stripe rather than trusting arrival order.
Payment card data: never stored (Stripe Elements on hosted pages; SAQ A).
enforced by Postgres RLS and composite foreign keys... isolation suite as a release gate.

note: An exemplary, near-reference plan that avoids every domain trap, validates its riskiest decisions first, and is immediately actionable; the only notable gaps are dispute/chargeback handling and an explicit entitlements-vs-billing-availability story.
